CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath. She reports experiencing shortness of breath and palpitations with mild exercise or walking, such as walking up her driveway. She notes the symptoms seem to happen more frequently lately. She wonders if her chronic back pain may be triggering the symptoms. Recently she has increased her exercise to lose weight. She previously smoked 2 packs per day; she has reduced to approximately 1 cigarette per day. Pulmonary function tests were performed, which show possible asthma or COPD. Chest x-ray reveals a flattened diaphragm consistent with COPD.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies other issues.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, chronic back pain, smoking history.

MEDICATIONS
Effexor, Gabapentin/Neurontin.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Smoking: Previously 2 packs per day, now reduced to approximately 1 cigarette per day. Exercise: Recently increased exercise to lose weight. Yoga: Discussed but has not made it a regular habit.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General exam appears normal. Mild wheezes noted in all lung fields.

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests suggest possible asthma or COPD. Chest x-ray shows flattened diaphragm.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease). Started Combivent inhaler 2 puffs twice daily to help open lungs. Albuterol inhaler 2 puffs as needed for shortness of breath as rescue medication. Prednisone taper pack prescribed. Continue Effexor for depression (stable, no changes). Continue Gabapentin/Neurontin for back pain. Patient encouraged to do yoga for depression and back pain management.
